title: Security in Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Security in Christ means that the believer’s salvation is guarded by the power, promise, and faithfulness of God. Those who belong to Christ are kept by Him, not by their own strength.
summary: Security in Christ means that the believer’s salvation is guarded by the power, promise, and faithfulness of God. Those who belong to Christ are kept by Him, not by their own strength.
christFocus: Jesus Christ secures His people by His finished work, ongoing intercession, shepherding care, and resurrection power. The believer’s safety rests in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Security in Christ is closely related to assurance and perseverance, but its focus is the believer’s safety in the Savior. Christ does not save His people loosely or temporarily.

Jesus says that His sheep will never perish and that no one can snatch them from His hand. The Father’s hand and the Son’s hand are stronger than every enemy.

Security does not rest on the believer’s flawless grip on Christ. Believers are called to continue in faith, but their confidence rests on the God who guards them through faith for salvation.

This doctrine does not encourage careless living. Those secure in Christ are called to holiness, gratitude, obedience, and perseverance because they belong to the Lord who keeps them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Fear often tells believers that suffering, weakness, failure, accusation, spiritual attack, or death can separate them from Christ. Scripture answers that nothing can separate God’s people from His love in Christ Jesus.

This doctrine strengthens weary believers who feel fragile. Their salvation is not fragile because their Savior is not fragile. Christ keeps what He has purchased.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rest in Christ’s keeping power without becoming careless. When fear accuses you, return to God’s promises. When sin tempts you, remember that you belong to Christ. Walk in obedience as one guarded by grace and held by the Savior.
